key_insight: Constitutive-Set Mechanics replaces a single guessed material law with the whole admissible set, then uses the structure's own variational solve to certify robust bounds and identify which constitutive possibilities actually matter.
engineering_relevance: This gives designers a way to quantify uncertainty in structural response when tests do not uniquely determine the material law, improving reliability for components with sparse or biased experimental data.
method: Formulate mechanics on an admissible set of constitutive laws instead of one law.
Use the occupation measure of strains reached by the structure to build a support-function energy over the set.
Extract equilibrium-based certificates for worst-case response and constitutive inference, with tighter results under global minimization.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports demonstrations on linear elasticity, phase-field fracture, a finite-strain composite shell, and a membrane case where the certified worst-case energy exceeded the reference by more than fourfold.
watch_item: The framework depends on the admissible constitutive set and on solving equilibrium problems accurately, so practical use may be sensitive to how that set is defined and how well the solver explores the relevant state space.
paper_title: Constitutive-Set Mechanics: variational mechanics on an admissible set of constitutive laws
